comment: Student plan going up a dollar to $6.99 stings when you're paying loans. It's still cheaper than most, I guess, but these yearly bumps add up fast.
Family plan is still way cheaper per person than anything else for us. Two extra bucks a month for five accounts is fine by me.
That's it, I'm out. Second hike in a couple of years and the app keeps getting worse. Going to free for now and I'm not looking back.
Apple Music is $10.99 for the individual plan and I already pay for iCloud. Moving over this week since Spotify wants more for less.
Didn't even read the email, I'm on a family plan through work so my card doesn't see this.
Honestly the line about benefiting artists is worth something. A dollar more a month is nothing next to what per-stream rates pay out.
Still no lossless after all these years and now they want more money. Tidal and Apple have had it forever, so this is hard to swallow.
Moving from Duo down to Individual. My partner barely uses it, so $18.99 for two accounts isn't worth it anymore.
YouTube Music Premium comes bundled with YouTube Premium, which I already have. Moving everything over there and dropping Spotify.
I mostly listen to podcasts anyway, so the price is still fine for what I get out of it.
Rather than pay this I'll go back to downloading. Spotify made their bed, they can sleep in it without my money.
Going to the free tier with ads. I'll deal with the ads since I can't justify paying this much right now.
Everything's going up, Netflix, Disney, all of them. This is just the new normal and I'm not surprised.
Still the best music app for the price and they keep investing in it. Happy to pay the new rate.
The redesign moved everything around and now they want more money for it. Fix the UI before raising prices.
Went to Tidal for the HiFi and it's the same price for lossless now. Done with Spotify for good.
Can't justify $12.99 with rent going up. Cancelling and I'll listen to the radio like it's 2005.
Ugh. Fine. Still staying but I'm grumbling about it.
Amazon Music Unlimited is cheaper if you already have Prime, and I do. Switching the family over this month.
I think a dollar more is reasonable. Labels take most of the money anyway, so Spotify isn't the villain here.
Didn't know about this until today. Honestly it's not going to change anything for me.
Duo going up almost two bucks for a plan that already splits badly. Feels like a shakedown.
Canceling tonight. Every price hike and still no HiFi, and the app keeps getting worse. I'm done.
Annoying but expected. Every other streamer went up too, so this doesn't really surprise me.
Starting an Apple Music trial today since the price keeps climbing. Lots of people I know are doing the same.
Didn't even notice the email. Spotify is still the one I want, so I'm not making a fuss about it.
Kids moved out so we're dropping from Family to Duo. Saving money that way makes the price hike hurt less.
Artist pay is the excuse every time. Artists will see a few cents more while the execs take the rest of the money.
